persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
When **US** jobs came in far below forecast, Bora Özkent sees it as good news for markets because the odds of an October hike fell to 22%; yet Treasury yields kept rising, and in his view the link between yields and inflation has broken. On **oil** he says Hormuz transits are nearing pre-war levels, Aramco is cutting prices in Asia and he expects crude to decline.

He is bearish on Europe: the **euro** is at a 17-month low and, given events in France and rising yields, he recommends staying away from European stocks. By contrast, with Bolsonaro finishing first in Brazil's first round he expects a good day for **Brazil** investors. He sees little effect from the US midterms and does not consider the Fed minutes very important.

items.title: Petrol Krizi Bitiyor mu?
items.summary: Bora Özkent reports US payrolls at 29K (forecast 84K), 60K jobs wiped from July-August and unemployment up to 4.2%, which he calls a 'Goldilocks' setup. The odds of an October hike fell to 22%, yet Treasury yields rose another 4 bps and in his view the link between yields and inflation has broken. With Hormuz transits nearing pre-war levels and Aramco pricing about $5 below the market in Asia, he expects crude to fall, though pump prices may lag because of refinery problems. Manufacturing PMI is strong at 58.7 and spending is growing 6.1% nominal year over year; he does not expect an abrupt drop in yields. He does not find Wednesday's Fed minutes very important and says a December hike is still on the table. He notes October is historically not a bad month, the election's effect will be small and only a full Democratic sweep could pressure AI stocks. The euro is at a 17-month low; given events in France and rising yields he argues for staying away from European stocks. Bolsonaro edged ahead of Lula in the first round and some Brazil ETFs were up about 10% in early trading.

assets.note: Expects crude to fall as Hormuz transits normalize.
Treasury yields rose 4 bps despite the jobs data; he expects some easing but not a sharp drop.
The euro is at a 17-month low.
Brazil ETFs were up about 10% early after Bolsonaro's lead; he foresees good days for Brazil investors.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies
holdings.opinion: At 21% it is the portfolio's largest position; at this concentration rate levels and credit-quality news will drive the stock.
ai_points: In favor: as growth continues it contributes the most to the portfolio.
Against: 21% concentration in one stock and Treasury yields continuing to rise (Bora Özkent) add risk.

holdings.name: Meta Platforms A

mentions.quote: At Meta, Claude Code users have roughly halved to ~30,000 from ~60,000 earlier this year.
$MSFT $META According to a report by The Information, Meta and Microsoft have begun restricting internal use of Anthropic's Claude model.

holdings.why: Two sources relayed that Meta is cutting Claude use but gave no view on the stock.
holdings.opinion: Cutting Claude use signals a shift to its own AI tools; the real question is whether that investment turns into revenue.
ai_points: In favor: shifting to in-house AI tools may reduce external spend.
Against: the payoff of AI spending is unclear and per BOJ's Uchida a sharp correction is possible if expected profits fail to arrive.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthropic’s lease of Google-designed AI chips supplied through Broadcom $AVGO, the largest chip-financing deal to date.
Under the deal Broadcom will provide up to $42B of debt financing to Anthropic for computing infrastructure and chip supply.

holdings.why: According to wallstengine the $42B Broadcom-backed senior debt went to bank syndication; sources relayed news, not a view.
holdings.opinion: Financing the customer supports demand but raises counterparty risk and the 'financing circle' debate.
ai_points: In favor: huge chip demand and financing capacity strengthen its position.
Against: the $42B Broadcom-backed debt carries counterparty risk on its balance sheet.

holdings.name: BWX Technologies
holdings.opinion: The nuclear supply-chain theme is supported by AI power demand; Goldman's data-center power forecast (64 GW in 2026) feeds it.
ai_points: In favor: per Goldman US data-center power demand grows 38% in 2026 and 2027.
Against: an 11% weight ties it to a single theme and rising yields may pressure valuation.

holdings.name: Reddit A
holdings.opinion: As an ad-revenue platform it is sensitive to AI traffic and market risk appetite; at 10% it is one of the portfolio's riskier positions.
ai_points: In favor: per Bora Özkent the US economy is lively and consumption strong, which supports ad spending.
Against: Ahmet Sunelcan finds ad companies too competitive for the long term.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: Treasury yields did not fall. On the contrary, they rose another 4 basis points.
The rise in US 10-year yields is worrying but still within critical limits.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent Treasury yields keep rising; however no concrete sell trigger (level, date) was given.
holdings.opinion: A long-duration bond fund is hurt directly by rising yields; climbing yields keep pressuring its price.
ai_points: In favor: per Bora Özkent weak jobs and falling oil could pull yields down somewhat.
Against: per the same source no abrupt drop in yields is expected as the economy stays lively.
